subject: DPA: subprocessor notice window, objection flow & e-sign preference
messages:
From: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@acmecloud.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA: Subprocessors, notice window & e-sign preference

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the heads-up on the DPA — attaching our redlines (see DPA_Acme_Redwood_v3.docx). Two quick, high-level asks from Acme legal/procurement before we proceed to e-sign:

1) Notice window for new subprocessors: your standard DPA currently references a 45-day notification window. For our risk model we need a 30-calendar-day minimum, or an explicit carve for high-risk processors to be 30 days.

2) Objection process: we want clarification on the objection timeline and remedies. Our proposed language is a 21-calendar-day objection window after notice, with right to require mitigation/removal if we mutually can’t resolve.

3) E-sign: we prefer DocuSign envelopes (tight integration with our procurement flow). If Redwood uses AdobeSign by default, can you confirm you can send via DocuSign?

Also copying Acme legal and procurement on the thread. Please advise next steps and whether Redwood can accept a 30-day notice or if you can propose alternate mitigations.

Attachments: DPA_Acme_Redwood_v3.docx

Thanks,
Jordan Miller
Head of Platform Partnerships
Acme Cloud

--

Subject: Re: DPA: subprocessor notice window, objection flow & e-sign preference

Thanks Jordan — appreciate the clear asks. I’ve looped in Karthik (legal) and Mina (security/compliance). High-level response from Redwood below and an attached draft with suggested compromise language (see attached DPA_Acme_Redwood_v3.docx and Subprocessor_List_20270601.csv).

- Notice window: Redwood’s standard practice is a 45-calendar-day general notice for additions to the subprocessor list. That gives customers time to review and, where necessary, negotiate mitigations. We can make a one-time concession for Acme to a 30-calendar-day notice for subprocessors that will process customer data categorized as non-sensitive. For processors handling higher-risk data classes (e.g., persistent PII, cross-border transfer functions), we’d retain 45 days or propose an expedited review path.

- Objection process: we propose a two-tier path: 1) 14-calendar-day objection window from notice to notify Redwood of material concerns; 2) if the parties don’t resolve within 21 calendar days from Redwood’s receipt of the objection, the parties escalate to specified contacts (see clause) and Redwood will provide either a mitigation plan or, if mitigation is not possible, offer removal or alternative routing where feasible. We prefer a shorter initial window to limit operational uncertainty.

- Emergency/critical changes: for urgent security patches or mitigations we will provide an "expedited notice" (minimum 72 hours) and a reasonable operational mitigation; these are limited to security incidents and critical infrastructure updates.

- E-sign: we default to DocuSign envelopes for commercial contracts. We can send the DocuSign envelope for the final DPA. If procurement requires AdobeSign, we can do that on a case-by-case basis but DocuSign is the standard.

Next steps: please review the attached redline. If you can accept the 30-day concession for defined low-risk processors and the objection/escrow path above, we’ll prepare a DocuSign envelope for signature. If you prefer alternate wording, Karthik can propose clean clause language.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA_Acme_Redwood_v3.docx; Subprocessor_List_20270601.csv

Priya — thanks for the quick reply and for the concession on low-risk processors. A few clarifying points from Acme legal: 

- We want the 30-day passage to be explicitly calendar days and apply to any processor that may access or store Acme customer data (we'll provide a risk flag per processor in the CSV).

- For the objection timeline, Acme prefers 21-calendar-days to notify of objections (not 14), given internal procurement cycles. If Redwood can commit to an escalation cadence (e.g., VP Legal within 7 days of unresolved objections) and a commitment to reasonable mitigation timelines, we should be able to accept the 30-day baseline.

- Audit rights: we need a clause confirming Redwood will facilitate evidence collection for scoped audits (SOC 2 reports / control narratives) for subprocessors on the critical list.

If you can confirm (1) 30-calendar-day notice for processors flagged as "customer-facing" or higher risk, (2) a 21-calendar-day objection window, and (3) DocuSign envelope, we'll move to signature.

Thanks,
Jordan

Subject: RE: DPA: subprocessor notice window, objection flow & e-sign preference

Jordan / Priya — thanks. Quick legal response and a proposed compromise clause below. I’ve kept it tight so procurement can accept without a lengthy loop.

Proposed compromise (suggested clause text):
"Notice and Objection to Subprocessor Additions: Redwood will provide Customer with written notice of any new subprocessor at least forty-five (45) calendar days prior to engaging the subprocessor. For subprocessors classified by Redwood as 'low risk' and listed in Appendix X, the parties agree a thirty (30) calendar day notice will apply. Customer will have fourteen (14) calendar days from Redwood's notice to notify Redwood of any material objection to the new subprocessor and provide reasonable detail regarding the basis for the objection. If the parties are unable to resolve the objection within twenty-one (21) calendar days after Redwood's receipt of the objection, the parties will escalate to the parties' VP Legal contacts. In cases of critical security updates or emergency remediation, Redwood may provide expedited notice (minimum seventy-two (72) hours) with accompanying mitigation steps and will work with Customer to minimize disruption."

Notes:
- We moved the customer's initial objection window to 14 days (not 21) to limit operational hold-ups; however, we're comfortable with a 21-day resolution period before escalation.
- We will include a specific audit evidence commitment for critical subprocessors (deliver SOC2 Type II or equivalent evidence within reasonable requests and subject to NDAs).
- DocuSign: confirm — Redwood will send via DocuSign.

If Acme insists on a 21-day initial objection period rather than 14, we can accept that as a one-time concession tied to the ACME-2027-015 deal, subject to executive sign-off (Karthik / Priya).

If you agree to the language above, I'll prepare a clean exhibit and we can send a DocuSign envelope this morning.

-Karthik
General Counsel (acting)
Redwood Inference
